titre: Canceled Mass Effect Addressed Squad Members’ Fates, Writer Reveals
chapo: A writer on the canceled Mass Effect: Universe hinted at how the game would handle returning characters and Mass Effect 3's ending.
extrait: Universe would have likely featured more returning characters beyond Liara Following the cancellation of the fifth mainline Mass Effect game, Mass Effect: Universe, fans can't help but wonder what could have been. In a recent Reddit AMA, Universe writer Cat Valente answered questions about the sequel, including how it would have addressed squad mates’ fates and Mass Effect 3’s controversial endings. Valente is an award-winning sci-fi and fantasy author and a Mass Effect series veteran, having previously written the 2018 novel Mass Effect: Annihilation. She worked on Universe for three years. While Valente was clear that she had to avoid certain specifics when discussing the canceled Mass Effect: Universe to avoid breaking NDAs, she hinted at which characters from previous Mass Effect titles would likely have appeared in the game. Universe would have been set 600 years after the original Mass Effect trilogy, but since certain species, like Asari and Krogan, can live 1,000 years or more, many characters from Mass Effect 3 could still be alive. Based on a leaked trailer, we already knew Liara T’Soni would appear in the game, but Valente hinted that other characters likely would as well. “I think the best way to answer your question is to say that any character who physically *could* survive, we considered allowing to survive into the new game and made decisions on them,” Valente said. “We thought about all the things you’d have wanted us to think about, and I hope you do believe that, because it’s the truth. Everyone in that room loved those characters, or loved to hate them, as much as any fan. We took each and every one of them and their fates very seriously.” Humans, Salarians, Turians, and Quarians don’t live long enough to survive for 600 years, so these characters were out of contention for a return. Beyond Liara, Grunt could certainly have appeared in Universe, as Krogan can live for centuries, and he was “only” a few hundred years old. Wrex is much less likely, given that he was implied to be close to a thousand years old already, and the same goes for the Asari Samara, but it's still possible in both cases. It’s unclear how the game would have handled synthetics like EDI, given how the ending of Mass Effect 3 hinges on the player’s choice about how to handle coexistence between organics and machine life. titre: Mass Effect Universe Would Have Answered Trilogy Ending Questions and Squadmate Fates, Writer Says
chapo: BioWare's canceled Mass Effect Universe would have addressed Mass Effect 3's controversial endings and the fates of Shepard's squadmates.
extrait: BioWare's canceled Mass Effect Universe would have addressed Mass Effect 3's controversial endings and the fates of Shepard's squadmates, one of the game's writers has said. For more than a decade, Mass Effect fans have debated how BioWare could reconcile the wildly divergent endings of Mass Effect 3 — and satisfy players who insisted that their particular ending choice should be canon (I see you, Destroy fans). But according to one of the writers behind the now-canceled Mass Effect Universe, the studio had actually cracked the puzzle before EA scrapped the project and closed BioWare forever. Speaking during a reddit fan Q&A supporting the "Save Mass Effect" fan movement, Mass Effect: Annihilation novel author Cat Valente — who spent three years on the writing team for the unfinished sequel — offered a bittersweet glimpse into how the narrative team approached the franchise's biggest lingering questions. While strict NDAs signed with published EA continue to prevent Valente from revealing specific plot details, she emphasized that reconciling Mass Effect 3's endings was front and center for the game's writers room, and noted that the team wasn't relying on a single silver bullet to bridge the 600-year narrative gap between the original trilogy and this upcoming fifth installment. "[We] worked specifically, and for a very long and laborious time, on handling the endings in a way that wouldn't piss everyone off, at least not piss them off completely, that wouldn't make them feel like nothing mattered, wouldn't privilege any one kind of player over another, but also allow us, somehow, to actually write a coherent story going forward, within the limits of having to do it in a playable mainstream video game and not a post-modern 3000 page novel," Valente wrote. "Not for nothing, guys, but that's *kind of a tall f***ing order*. Part of the reason it took so long and Andromeda was in Andromeda is that figuring out an elegant solution to that problem turns out to be *really hard.* An elegant solution that we can do with current game tech, that will be approved by higher-ups, that doesn't take over the whole game and make actually telling a story impossible... it takes a long time, and it's not obvious how best to pull it off when you're the people who bear responsibility for pulling off one of, if not the, hardest nut to crack in game writing.
